Tinnitus

Five animal studies include rat and mouse tinnitus models. They provide mechanistic or preclinical findings only and do not establish clinical benefit.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Five animal studies include rat and mouse tinnitus models. They provide mechanistic or preclinical findings only and do not establish clinical benefit.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Tinnitus and Tinnitus plus hearing-loss mappings contain 40 unique titles. They include 31 human publications, five animal studies, and five reviews or meta-analyses; one 2024 publication contains both human and mouse arms, so evidence-type totals overlap. Human records include 22 randomized reports, eight other controlled or single-arm reports, and one case series. Reviews reuse the underlying trials.

Human and clinical evidence

Results are mixed. In a 56-person trial of 830-nm TINI treatment, the final between-group tinnitus-score difference from sham was not significant, although some within-group measures improved (Choi et al. 2024). A separate 38-person single-blind placebo-controlled study reported improvement in selected emotional and loudness/perception subscales after eight sessions over four weeks, without establishing long-term benefit (Choi et al. 2025). A 20-person triple-blind trial found improvements in tinnitus VAS and selected THI measures when PBM was added to vestibular rehabilitation; dizziness and disability improved in both groups without a between-group difference (de Góes et al. 2026). A 2020 meta-analysis found no statistically significant pooled difference from control (Chen et al. 2020). These findings do not establish a consistent effect across tinnitus presentations.

Animal evidence

Five animal records include two rat and three mouse studies. They model tinnitus-related injury or auditory processing and examine selected behavioral or biological outcomes. Animal evidence remains indirect and does not resolve the mixed patient results.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro study was identified in the mapped category records.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The records include varied laser and LED approaches, transcranial or local treatment, and PBM combined with vestibular rehabilitation. Session numbers and follow-up vary. The 830-nm study and the adjunctive rehabilitation trial are not interchangeable, and improvement during a treatment course does not establish a durable effect. Tinnitus scales and subscales also differ among studies.

Interpretation

There is a possible short-term signal for selected outcomes in some protocols, but null sham-controlled results, a negative pooled estimate, and varied interventions keep certainty low. The evidence does not support a general claim for PBM monotherapy or sustained tinnitus relief.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for short-term improvement in selected tinnitus outcomes with adjunctive protocols Very low for durable benefit or PBM monotherapy across tinnitus populations
Publications and records40 unique titles across the two mapped categories.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The database maps 40 unique titles, including 31 human reports, but populations, devices, and outcomes vary. A large sham-controlled study found no significant final between-group tinnitus-score difference, while smaller reports show selected subscale or adjunctive-treatment benefits. A meta-analysis found no significant pooled advantage. Cohort overlap and short follow-up limit confidence.
